name: speech-to-text

advert.what: Hear speech and return text. whisper.cpp on the CPU, fed 16 kHz mono WAV by ffmpeg, with a declared model so a bigger box only needs a bigger file. The ear that goes with the mouth on :8144.
advert.time: about 10 s for a 3 s clip on 4 CPU threads with the tiny.en model; larger models trade time for accuracy

provider.name: whisper.cpp
provider.update: download a newer whisper.cpp release, or a better ggml model — the service declaration does not change
provider.note: The model is an INIT variable, not part of the service: ggml-tiny.en.bin is the default so a GPU-less node works out of the box, and a node with a card points the same service at a bigger file.

whenItDoesNotFit: A machine without ffmpeg cannot decode input, and a machine without whisper-cli cannot recognise it — both are reported as MISSING with the path that was looked for, never as "no speech detected". Silence and a broken install must not read the same way.

progress.how: stt.ps1 runs one recogniser pass and prints a single JSON line when it is done, so progress is "waiting for one line": there is no partial text to report and claiming otherwise would be noise.

output.shape: { ok, text, ms, model, threads, chars }

pages.ad:
Hear speech, return text

The mouth has been real for a while — text to speech runs on this node already. This is the ear, and it is the cheap half on purpose: whisper.cpp on the CPU, so the machine with no graphics card still gets a voice.

Why it is a service and not a script

Because the fleet should be able to ask for it the same way it asks for anything else. A node advertises "I can transcribe", a broker or a Scheduler books it, and the answer comes back as text. A tool that only one person knows how to run is not infrastructure.

What it needs

No GPU. About 1.2 GB of RAM and two cores. ffmpeg on the box to decode, whisper-cli and a ggml model in place. That is all — a four-core machine with 8 GB can hold this and still answer.

The two answers it refuses to confuse

A missing model says MISSING model and the path it looked for. A quiet room says no speech. Those two sentences look alike to a careless tool, and telling them apart is the difference between a service you can trust and one that quietly lies.
pages.inputs:
Transcribe an audio file

One file in, the words out. Any container ffmpeg understands — the conversion to the 16 kHz mono WAV the recogniser wants is done for you.

During a run this page carries the progress: one recogniser pass, one JSON line back. There is no partial text to show, and inventing a progress bar that moves on its own would be worse than waiting.
